source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the temporal setting, Jesus’ knowledge, departure, belonging, and the phrase that can mean both to the end and utterly.
key_decisions.before: Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew his hour had come to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.
key_decisions.after: Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that his hour had come to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the very end.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that his hour had come to depart from this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Peter’s emphatic refusal and Jesus’ condition about participation with him.
key_decisions.before: Peter said, “You will certainly never wash my feet!” Jesus answered, “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.”
key_decisions.after: Peter said to him, “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus answered, “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Peter said to him, “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus answered him, “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the distinction between bathing and footwashing and the ominous qualification.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said, “The one who has bathed does not need to wash except the feet but is completely clean. And you are clean—but not all of you.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus said to him, “Someone who has bathed needs only to wash his feet, but is completely clean. And you are clean—but not all of you.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to him, “One who has bathed does not need to wash, except for the feet, but is entirely clean. And you are clean—though not all of you.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the limitation, election, fulfillment, shared bread, and hostile heel image.
key_decisions.before: “I am not speaking about all of you. I know those I have chosen. But Scripture must be fulfilled: ‘The one eating my bread has lifted his heel against me.’
key_decisions.after: I am not speaking about all of you. I know those I have chosen. But the Scripture must be fulfilled: ‘The one who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But it is to fulfill the scripture, ‘The one who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me.’

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the beloved disciple’s identification and meal posture without importing a name.
key_decisions.before: One of his disciples, the one Jesus loved, was reclining close beside Jesus.
key_decisions.after: One of his disciples—the one Jesus loved—was reclining beside Jesus.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: One of his disciples—the one Jesus loved—was reclining close to Jesus.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the sequence, Satan’s entry, and Jesus’ urgent command without recasting its agency.
key_decisions.before: After Judas took the piece, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do quickly.”
key_decisions.after: After Judas took the piece of bread, Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do quickly.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Then after the morsel, Satan entered into him. Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do quickly.”

key_decisions.rationale: Renders the variant-marked main-text clause and preserves reciprocal and immediate glorification.
key_decisions.before: If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself and will glorify him immediately.
key_decisions.after: If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him at once.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him at once.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves command, mutuality, and Jesus’ love as the measure.
key_decisions.before: I give you a new commandment: love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also must love one another.
key_decisions.after: I give you a new commandment: love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also must love one another.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: I give you a new commandment: that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.
